text: To do something dismally is to do it very badly, so badly that people feel gloomy. Here, the test scores were a big letdown.
A budding engineer is someone just starting out who may grow into a great one, like a plant bud that will open into a flower.
To weather something means to get safely through a hard time, like a house that stands up to a storm. It is not about rain here.
An Olympiad is a big contest, named after the Olympic Games. This one is for school robots instead of sports.
Gloomy means sad and without hope, like a dark, cloudy day. The parents expect the future to go badly.
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is computer software that can do things that usually need a human mind, like understanding speech or solving problems.
To destroy something is to break it so badly it cannot be used again. Here, people fear AI will wipe out jobs.
A region is a large area of the world. Here it means Latin America, a group of many countries.
International means involving many countries. These tests compare students from around the world.
Astonishing means so surprising it is hard to believe. The article means huge changes that no one saw coming.
Thrilled means very excited and happy about something.
Pockets of excellence are small places where things work very well, even though the rest of the system does not. A few great schools in a weak school system are an example.
Reformers are people who work to change something to make it better, such as a school system.
Enthusiasm is strong, excited interest in something.
A glimpse is a quick look. The writer says the Olympiad gives a quick peek at what is possible.
An arena is a big indoor building for sports and concerts, with seats all around.
Candombe is a style of drumming and music from Uruguay, played on tall drums with a strong beat.
To program a robot is to give it exact instructions on what to do. The kids wrote the instructions their robots follow.
To whizz is to move very fast with a buzzing sound, like a racing toy car.
A drone is a small flying machine with no pilot on board. It is steered by a remote control or a computer.
Obstacles are things in the way that you must get around, like cones in a race.
Here, beams means smiles very widely and happily. It can also mean a ray of light.
A correspondent is a reporter who sends stories from a place. Here, the writer is talking about themself.
To loom is to rise up large and tall over something. A giant picture looms over the kids.
Pupils are students in a school. In the article it has nothing to do with the eye.
Twenty-fold means twenty times as big. If a team count went from 10 to 200, it grew 20-fold.
A micro:bit is a tiny computer about the size of a credit card, with little lights on it. Kids can program it to do simple tasks.
An LED is a small light that uses very little power, like the tiny lights on a gadget.
Attracting here means pulling people in, so that more and more of them join.
A shindig is a lively party or big event. It is a playful word.
State-funded means paid for by the government with tax money.
A 3D printer is a machine that builds a solid object, layer by layer, from a computer design.
Computational thinking is breaking a big problem into small steps, the way a computer would.
To spark something is to start it, like a spark that lights a fire. Here, it means starting a love of learning.
Ambitions are big goals that you really want to reach.
STEM stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math, the subjects used to build and understand things.
A university is a school you go to after high school to study more, also called college.
Pollsters are people who ask many people their opinions to learn what groups think.
